summary: Real Estate Investment Analysis and Portfolio Management Training for property professionals. Build DCF models, risk registers, and portfolio scorecards.
lede: Real estate investment analysis and portfolio management provides a structured way to evaluate property assets using financial models, market evidence, and portfolio metrics. This course develops practical skills in discounted cash flow modelling, cap rate comparison, lease-based cash flow analysis, and sensitivity testing to support disciplined acquisition, disposal, and financing decisions. You will create acquisition appraisals, portfolio scorecards, risk registers, and investment memorandums while reviewing diversification, concentration, vacancy exposure, and portfolio performance. You will also explore PropTech-enabled market scanning and AI-assisted portfolio screening at an operational level, helping you frame what to buy, hold, improve, refinance, or sell.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage property investments, evaluate returns, or prepare portfolio decisions in commercial, residential, or mixed asset settings. Real Estate Investment Analysts who underwrite acquisitions and compare cash flow scenarios. Portfolio Managers who rebalance property holdings and track concentration risk. Asset Managers who monitor NOI, vacancy, and capital expenditure performance. Acquisition Specialists who evaluate deal pipelines and prepare investment cases. Commercial Property Finance Managers who structure debt and equity decisions. Real Estate Valuation Analysts who test assumptions in income models. Investment Committee Secretaries who prepare evidence packs and board papers. Development Finance Managers who assess feasibility and exit assumptions. Facilities and Property Managers who feed operational data into portfolio reviews. Corporate Real Estate Strategists who align holdings with occupancy and capital plans.
prerequisites: Bring a laptop with Microsoft Excel installed and a working understanding of NPV, IRR, and basic property valuation concepts. A calculator, prior exposure to investment appraisal, and familiarity with reading rental schedules or portfolio reports will help you move faster through the exercises.
